# Private Apple mapped block-map capacity workflow

This workflow builds the pinned private source and qualifies one owned Mainnet checkpoint on a standard native 7 GiB Apple Silicon runner. The fixture, storage verification, network isolation, and UTXO checks reuse the mature checkpoint harness. Earlier stock startup outcomes remain separate observations. Successful qualification covers the sealed checkpoint and its two level-4 passes.

The workflow trigger uses new private paths on the existing `ci/en8-apple-index-cache` branch to reuse the Darwin dependency cache. The currently defined Apple index-cache workflow watches different paths. The source build uses the existing Apple Silicon depends toolchain, a separate CMake configuration, the project’s global `APPEND_CXXFLAGS` diagnostic flag, and the daemon and required tests. The compile database must show the private ABI flag on every C++ translation unit. The transfer contains the exact source and tree, compile audit, daemon and test runner with SHA-256 checks. The native job verifies the thin arm64 binaries and required system libraries, applies ad-hoc signatures, verifies those signatures, and runs the selected regression suites.

The native job applies `qualifier.patch` to its disposable checkout. It verifies the existing public manifest before fetching the nine archive parts. The minimum initial capacity is 36,954,082,365 bytes, covering the complete compressed archive, its verified extraction, the physical arena extent and 8 GiB free space. The qualifier rechecks extraction headroom on the current runner and the diagnostic rechecks APFS space before and after reserving the physical extent. The prior 25.748 GiB sampled minimum was recorded after the fixture was already present. The current run measures available space at each relevant phase.

The daemon receives the profile opt-in only in its child process. The native harness requires the ordered reservation and completed allocation log records for 44,946,269 nodes, 34,310 mapped chunks and one bootstrap heap chunk. It uses the full 480-second startup allowance or records a prelaunch budget refusal. It requires the exact checkpoint tip, two complete level-four passes, the pinned UTXO state, and a clean owned shutdown. The mapped profile uses a 60-second graceful stop limit and bounded signal escalation. Fresh startup and controlled shutdown timings remain separate.

Resource evidence includes process CPU/RSS, physical footprint, Darwin process page-ins and disk I/O counters, host compressor and swap/page activity, sampled free space, bounded owned-PID VM-map summaries, and startup/link/teardown markers. Per-process disk I/O attribution can omit delayed kernel activity on dirty mappings. Raw receipts retain refused, partial and timed-out trials. A verified checkpoint run does not measure fresh Mainnet synchronization time.

The intended preflight is the exact pinned-source workflow branch, with the private source SHA reachable on the CI repository. A source review amendment requires synchronized workflow and tooling pins. Review and publish the workflow through the existing CI branch with a fast-forward update.
